 Richard Glossip, Oklahoma man on death row for years, pleads guilty to lesser charge
 By Eric Levenson , Brynn Gingras 
 Updated Nov 12, 2026, 4:33 PM ET 
 PUBLISHED Nov 12, 2026, 2:53 PM ET 
 Richard Glossip stands before a hearing at the Oklahoma County Courthouse on June 23 in Oklahoma City. 
 Nate Billings/AP 
 Supreme Court

 Richard Glossip, the Oklahoma man who spent nearly 30 years on death row before his murder conviction was overturned by the US Supreme Court last year, pleaded guilty Thursday to accessory to murder after the fact, avoiding a third murder trial, his attorney told CNN.
 The plea agreement came during what was expected to be a pretrial hearing ahead of a retrial scheduled for December on a charge of first-degree murder.
 Instead, his sentencing is scheduled for December 17 and 18, his attorney said. His defense plans to ask for time served, while prosecutors said they intend to seek additional prison time.
 The guilty plea is the latest twist in a sprawling legal saga for Glossip, now 63, that stems from the 1997 killing of an Oklahoma City motel owner, Barry Van Treese.
 At two murder trials, Justin Sneed, a motel employee who admitted to killing Van Treese with a baseball bat, took the stand and testified Glossip, the motel manager, put him up to it as part of a murder-for-hire plot. Glossip was convicted and sentenced to death in 1998 — a conviction that was overturned because of ineffective defense counsel — and then again in 2004.
 Sneed received a life sentence in exchange for his testimony against Glossip.
 While on death row, Glossip was scheduled to be put to death nine times and was served three last meals but narrowly avoided execution. In 2015, his execution was stopped at the last minute by then-Gov. Mary Fallin after officials discovered a mix-up in a shipment of lethal injection drugs.
 Related article
 Former death row prisoner Richard Glossip, left, speaks to media after exiting a detention facility after being granted bond while awaiting retrial Thursday, May 14, 2026, in Oklahoma City. (AP Photo/Nick Oxford) 
 Nick Oxford/AP 
 A timeline of former death row inmate Richard Glossip’s legal battles spanning nearly 30 years 
 4 min read 
 But persistent questions about Sneed’s testimony and the lack of evidence linking Glossip to the crime led to a bipartisan investigation challenging the legitimacy of the conviction. In 2023, Oklahoma Attorney General Gentner Drummond, a Republican, moved to vacate Glossip’s conviction.
 Last year, the US Supreme Court in a split decision overturned the conviction and ordered a new trial, citing Sneed’s false testimony and the prosecution’s withholding of evidence from the defense.
 “We conclude that the prosecution violated its constitutional obligation to correct false testimony,” Justice Sonia Sotomayor wrote for the majority.
 Sneed has never publicly recanted his testimony. But Glossip’s legal team has produced witnesses who claim Sneed exonerated Glossip in private conversations, along with a handwritten note from prison in which he asks, “Do I have the choice of re-canting my testimony at anytime during my life, or anything like that.”
 Still, Drummond said last June his office planned to retry Glossip on a murder charge.
 As he awaited his third trial, Glossip was released on bond in May thanks to funds from the celebrity and criminal reform advocate Kim Kardashian .
 Glossip has maintained his innocence, attorney says
 Drummond said Thursday that accepting the lesser charge for Glossip was a “difficult decision,” according to CNN affiliate KOKH .
 “Today, Richard Glossip finally took some measure of responsibility for the murder of Barry Van Treese,” he said. “While allowing Glossip to plead guilty to the lesser-related charge of accessory to first-degree murder was a difficult decision for me, (and) more importantly, the Van Treese family, we both recognize that this path ensures a conviction related to Mr. Van Treese’s murder and gives us the best chance to secure additional prison time for Glossip.”

 Special counsel reviewing case of man on death row for 26 years
 4:30
 • Source:

 Special counsel reviewing case of man on death row for 26 years 
 4:30
 Don Knight, Glossip’s attorney, issued a statement reacting to the news.
 “For 30 years, Richard Glossip has maintained his innocence. After nearly executing him nine times, the State of Oklahoma has now dismissed the murder charge against him. This morning, to finally put this matter to rest, Rich pleaded guilty to being an accessory after the fact,” Knight said.
 “We believe Rich has more than paid his debt to society by spending nearly 30 years on death row, during which time he was served three last meals, and came within minutes of being executed for a crime he did not commit.”
 “In 1997, had Rich been given the longest possible sentence for the crime he pled guilty to today, he would never have been on death row and would have been released ten years ago,” Knight said. “We look forward to an opportunity to show why returning him to custody would not serve the interests of justice, and to ending this nightmare for Rich and all concerned.”
 Glossip spoke to CNN in 2023 about the difficulty of life on death row.
 “It’s one of the scariest things, especially if you’re an innocent person, to know they’re going to take your life for something you had nothing to do with,” Glossip told CNN in an exclusive interview during one of those phone calls.
 After his release on bond in May , Glossip told reporters he was thankful for his wife and attorneys and said he is “just really happy.”
 “It’s overwhelming, but it’s amazing at the same time,” he said.
 This story has been updated with additional information. 
 CNN’s Andy Rose contributed to this report.
